title: Understand the true statement
text: $$\log_2(3**4)=4\log_2(3)$$ is the law of logarithms for powers

title: Understand the true statement
text: $$\log_b(\sqrt{x})=\log_b(x**{1/2})=\frac{1}{2}\log_b(x)$$ is an example of the law of logarithms for powers where the power is $$\frac{1}{2}$$. This makes sense as long as the input $$x>0$$

title: Understand the true statement
text: $$\log_b(1)=\log_b(b**0)=0$$ for any valid base. A base is valid if $$b>0$$ and $$b\neq$$ $$1.$$

title: A common error
text: A common error is to assume the law of logarithms applies to an expression of the form $$(\log_2(3))**4.$$ It does not! The power must be inside the parentheses! This has no simplified form.
